Webbed feet step gently over the marsh lily pads as the lanky fennfi stle searches for its favored meal, eggs. Th is opportunistic ovivore 
keeps a gold-flecked eye out for either bird eggs nested within the rushes and cattails along the shore, or for the glimmerings of the 
ovoid shapes of amphibian and fi sh eggs beneath the surface. Its long sinuous neck perfectly adapted to quickly gulp down its prize 
into an expandable, horned gular and rush off before any protective parent or nearby predator can catch this nimble beast. With wide 
webbed toes and bounding jumps, it leaps across rivers and ponds. Th is amphibian is perfectly adapted to the damp environments of 
the Fenlands and can outpace any creature that ventures into its swampy home.

Toothed Gulp Melee Attack Roll: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. 
Hit: 12 (3d6+4) Piercing damage. Strength Saving Th row: DC 12, 
target Small or smaller creature that the fennfi stle has successfully 
hit with its Toothed Gulp. Failure: Th e target is swallowed. A 
swallowed creature has the Blinded and Restrained Condition, 
has Total Cover against attacks and other effects outside the 
fennfi stle , and takes 2 (1d6) Acid damage at the start of each of 
the fennfi stle ’s turns. If the fennfi stle takes 10 damage or more 
on a single turn from a creature inside it, the fennfi stle must 
succeed on a DC 16 Constitution Saving Th row at the end of that 
turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, each of which falls in 
a space within 5 ft. of the fennfi stle and has the Prone condition. 
If the fennfi stle dies, any swallowed creatures no longer have the 
Restrained condition and can escape from the corpse using 5 ft. 
of movement, exiting Prone. Th e fennfi stle can swallow up to 2 
Small creatures at a time.

Encountering Searching for such an elusive egg snatcher 
requires an equally clever hunter. As the amphibian is quite 
adept at traversing its watery environment, loud splashing 
sounds of incoming intruders often alerts it long before it can 
be spotted over the swaying cattails. Although the creature is 
known to be a sly hunter, it will not pass up an easy meal and a 
baited egg set in a clearing or rushes will get its attention.
A lithe body and strong nimble 
legs allow the amphibian to 
quickly evade predators over 
the muddy paths and shallow 
depths of the marshes
A long sinuous forked
